messages:
maria: FYI we have a customer (internal case 5421) seeing duplicate completions and unexpected billing spikes. They report a bunch of 502s and timeouts followed by repeated completions — looks retry-related. cc @devin @ash

maria: Quick summary from the ticket: their client got a 502 on a create-completion call, retried automatically, and ended up with 3 completions (charged each). They do NOT set any idempotency key today.

devin: ugh. Are they using our JS SDK default retry behavior or a custom client implementation?

maria: Using our JS SDK v2.4.0 default settings (no custom retry handler).

devin: OK. By default the SDK retries on network errors + 5xx up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff + full jitter. That is intended to reduce false failures, but for non-idempotent endpoints (create) it can cause duplicates if the server actually processed the first request but returned an error.

ash: Important context: our gateway returns 502 when a downstream model worker dies after response started but before the gateway acknowledges. In that case, the model may have generated a completion and charged the customer. The gateway loss makes the client think it failed. Retry after that => duplicate.

oliver: So root causes: (1) upstream partial success, (2) client retries without idempotency. Also token-bucket/quota bursts exacerbate it: a replay of retries across many clients can hit quota and then cascade.

maria: Customer wants mitigation recommendations and repro steps so they can audit. Also asked if we can change SDK defaults to be safer.

devin: Short-term mitigation for customers: add an Idempotency-Key header (UUID) on the create call. If you retry with the same key the server will dedupe. Example curl repro (no idempotency -> duplicates):

```bash
# initial request (no idempotency) - may return 502
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","prompt":"hello"}'
```

# retry in client (still no idempotency) -> duplicate completion likely
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","prompt":"hello"}'
```

# safe approach with idempotency
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 9f2b7de4-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-abcdef123456" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","prompt":"hello"}'
```

devin: SDK config snippet (Node) customers can set to be conservative immediately: reduce retries to 0 for "create" endpoints or enable idempotency token auto-injection. Example: 

```js
// pseudo-config
const client = new Redwood({
  maxRetries: 0, // disable automatic retries for non-idempotent calls
  idempotency: { auto: true } // experimental: auto-inject UUID for create endpoints
})
```

ash: From infra/SRE side, we should also consider gateway changes: accept Idempotency-Key header and dedupe server-side for X minutes, and add explicit response signals so clients can tell if a request actually succeeded (e.g., 202 with operation id).

oliver: We should also document guidance: non-idempotent endpoints should not be retried by default. Retries default is a footgun in face of partial success. Folks who need high availability should pair retries with idempotency.

devin: Proposal: for next SDK patch (v2.4.x) set default behavior to: maxRetries: 1, but only for idempotency-enabled requests; otherwise maxRetries=0 for create. And add a warning in console when creating a client without idempotency.

maria: Customer asked for repro steps to audit how many duplicates occurred and which calls were retried. We can provide logs if they give a request-id time window. We should give them a small script to correlate request timestamps with billing events.

ash: Repro script outline (internal, send to customer): query logs for the request id or IP + time window, look for repeated request bodies and compare server-side sequence numbers. Also check our billing ledger for repeated charge events in same minute.

maria: I'll prepare a short KB and the repro snippet for the customer. Also will offer to escalate to Premium support to get idempotency enabled server-side for their org while they migrate.

devin: I'll open a SDK PR to add an opt-in "safeMode" flag that defaults to off but we can toggle for affected customers. PR will include tests for not retrying non-idempotent endpoints and for auto idempotency header behavior.

ops-bot: deploy 2.4.1 -> canary deployed to staging at 2026-03-14T18:23:12Z :rocket:

maria: Thanks team — let's loop in Product if a server-side change is required. For now customer action items: set Idempotency-Key or set SDK maxRetries:0 for create calls. I'll send the KB and repro instructions to the customer.

devin: also add a sentence in SDK README about the billing risk when not using idempotency and when retrying. short & clear. :thumbsup:
